# 十住經

**ID:** T0286
**Volume:** T10
**Category:** 華嚴部類
**Original Category:** 華嚴部
**Byline:** 姚秦 鳩摩羅什譯
**Dynasty:** 姚秦
**Date:** 402–412
**Juans:** 4
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0286

## Contributors
- 鳩摩羅什 (A001583)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Shí zhù jīng* in 4 fascicles is [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) Kumārajīva's translation of the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra* — the second complete Chinese version of this fundamental bodhisattva-path text, after *[Zhú Fǎhù's Jiàn bèi yīqiè zhì dé jīng 漸備一切智德經](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0033)* (T0285) of the Western Jìn. It is conventionally regarded as the most stylistically polished of the Chinese translations, and (because of Kumārajīva's wide influence in subsequent Chinese Buddhism) was the basis for much of the *Daśabhūmika*-related doctrinal exegesis in the fifth- and sixth-century Chinese Buddhist tradition. The same material appears, in subtly different recensions, as chapter 22 of the *[60-fascicle Huáyán](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001)* and chapter 26 of the *[80-fascicle Huáyán](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010)*.

The opening reads: "*Huānxǐ dì* (Pramuditā), the first" (歡喜地第一) — the first of the ten *bhūmi*-stages — followed by the standard sūtra-opening "Thus have I heard" (如是我聞).

**Abstract**

[鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) Kumārajīva (Jīumóluóshí 鳩摩羅什, 344 – 413 CE — but more recent scholarship (Pelliot, Tsukamoto Zenryū, Lu Yang) refines the dates to ~344 – 413 with substantial uncertainty) was the most consequential translator of Mahāyāna Buddhist texts in Chinese history. Born in Kuchā 龜茲 (modern Kuqa, Xinjiang) of an Indian Brahmin father and a Kuchanese princess mother, he was abducted to Liángzhōu 涼州 by the warlord Lü Guāng 呂光 in 384 and held there for nearly two decades, until in 401 he was conveyed to Cháng'ān by Yáo Xìng 姚興 of the Later Qín. Between 402 and 413 he led the great Cháng'ān translation bureau that produced the *Lotus Sūtra* (*Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, T0262), the *Vimalakīrti-sūtra* (T0475), the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-mahāvibhāṣā* (T1521), the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* (大智度論, T1509), the *Madhyamaka-śāstra* (中論, T1564), and many others. The *Shí zhù jīng* belongs to this corpus.

The translation is conventionally dated to the early years of Kumārajīva's Cháng'ān bureau, c. 402 – 409 CE; the bracket adopted here reflects this window. The team included [僧叡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E5%8F%A1) Sēngrúi, [僧肇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E8%82%87) Sēngzhào, [道融](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E8%9E%8D) Dàoróng, and [竺道生](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E9%81%93%E7%94%9F) Zhú Dàoshēng — all of whom would become major Buddhist figures in their own right.

The text is one of the most important sources for the doctrine of the ten bodhisattva stages (*daśabhūmi*) in the Chinese Buddhist tradition; it was one of the texts whose translation by [勒那摩提](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8B%92%E9%82%A3%E6%91%A9%E6%8F%90) Ratnamati and [菩提流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) Bodhiruci into the *Shídì jīng lùn* 十地經論 ([KR6e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0060), T1522, the *Daśabhūmika-vyākhyāna* of Vasubandhu) founded the *Dìlùn* 地論 school of the Northern Wèi, and indirectly the Chinese Huáyán school. Modern scholarship (Hamar 2007, Liú 2009) treats Kumārajīva's *Shí zhù jīng* as the linguistic-doctrinal benchmark against which all later Chinese versions of the *Daśabhūmika* (including those embedded in T0278 and T0279) must be assessed.

The Taishō text (T0286) is established on the standard apparatus including the *Sēn* 森 (Senno-ji) Japanese alternate witness, an unusually rich apparatus reflecting the work's continuing scholastic importance.
